  - a disc: a central hub plus one or two rings cut into wedges

pieces.gap: Hiding spots are not safe, and hiding was one of Joe's three explicit asks. There are two causes. (1) In level.js tryGen, hiding spots (L.shades) are placed before placeGuards, so about 30% of them land on a patrol route. The guard walks through the shade and the player is caught (F6 seed 11: guard came within 1-15 units in 4 of 4 shades; F10 seed 33: 3 of 4). (2) In game.js sees(), a guard senses anything within 26 units in every direction, even a hidden player (`if (near && d < 26) return {d}` runs before the hidden check). Hidden players are also seen normally inside 30 units (`if (P.hidden && d > 30) return null`), and updateGuard sets aw=1 instantly when s.d<28. A guard that loses you as you enter a shade walks to the last spot it saw you, which is the shade's rim, about 17-22 units from the centre, and catches you there: 4 of 4 caught on floors 3/5/6/9. Fix: (a) in game.js sees(), replace those two lines with `if (P.hidden) return d < 12 ? { d } : null;` placed before the near check, so a hidden player is only found by actually bumping into them (CATCH 16 still applies). (b) In chase/search, when the last-seen point is inside a shade (L.shades.some(s => dist < s.r)), move the search target 30 units back along the guard-to-target line, so the guard stops at the rim and looks around rather than standing on the player. (c) In level.js, move the hiding-spot loop to after placeGuards(R, L, field, navClosed, n). Reject any candidate whose centre is within s.r + 30 (about 50 units) of any guard path segment (sample each segment every 8 units), of a sentry's home, or of the entrance/exit. Keep the 80-try loop and the existing want counts. Then add a hide-and-chase case to tools/ai-check.mjs (get chased, enter a shade, expect search then return rather than caught).

pieces.gap: The camera has no lookahead in practice. In updateView (stealth/js/game.js about lines 494-500) the target is tx = P.x + P.vx*0.32, smoothed with rate 4. At a steady speed v, exponential follow lags by v/rate = 0.25v, so the net lead is 0.32v - 0.25v = 0.07v: about 9 world px (7-10 screen px) at the 128 px/s run. Measured: after 3s of running right or down, the player's screen position moved only -6 to -10px in both portrait and landscape. Running into a cone you can't see is the main way a player gets caught unfairly on a phone, especially running vertically in landscape (only 245 world px visible ahead against cones up to 190 long). Fix: (1) In updatePlayer after field.move, keep a measured velocity, e.g. P.avx += ((P.x-before.x)/dt - P.avx)*(1-Math.exp(-dt*10)) and the same for P.avy, so the lead follows real motion and not thumb intent. (2) In updateView keep a separate smoothed lead vector: leadTarget = (P.avx, P.avy)*0.6, magnitude capped at min(W,H)/view.z*0.28 (about 130 world px on a phone); view.lead eases toward it at rate 2.5; then tx = P.x + view.lead.x, with the same for ty (plus the existing portrait +70/tz). Ease the base follow at rate 6-8 on (P.x + lead), not 4, so the lead is not eaten by lag. Target: when running steadily the player sits 60-100 screen px behind centre, opposite the direction of travel, and returns to centre within about 0.6s after stopping.

pieces.gap: The chase and suspicion rhythms fight each other. The heartbeat runs on its own clock in js/audio.js schedule(): `nextBeat += 1.05 - 0.55*curHeat(now)`, which is 57-120 bpm and never tied to the sequencer. In a chase, heat is 1, so a lub-dub at 120 bpm (two thuds every 0.5 s) plays at full beat-layer gain (2.0) on top of kick and toms pushed to 100 bpm. That is a 6:5 polyrhythm that drifts in and out of phase, and the heartbeat is the louder of the two (measured -14.6 dB vs -15.6 dB RMS). The suspicion heartbeat also drifts against the 84 bpm pulse (0.79 s per beat vs 0.714 s at heat 0.47). Fix: (a) Remove the free `nextBeat` loop from schedule() and play heart() inside play(s,t) on the grid, so it always follows stepDur and the chase tempo push. When heat < 0.5: lub on pos%8==0, dub one 16th later on pos%8==1 at v 0.6 (one beat per half bar, about 42 bpm at 84 BPM). When 0.5 <= heat < 0.85: lub on pos%4==0, dub on pos%4==1 (84 bpm). When heat >= 0.85: lub only, on pos%2==0. (b) Let the drums take over in a chase. In schedule(), change `layers.beat.gain.setTargetAtTime(lv(t,0.4,0.6)*2, ...)` to `lv(t,0.4,0.6)*2*(1-0.8*lv(t,0.78,0.92))`, so at T=1 the heartbeat sits about 14 dB down and the kick, toms and snare carry the pulse. Then gate the tremolo string the same way, or keep it as the only beat-layer element in a chase.

pieces.gap: A thumb that lands at or near the rim is held at a walk and has to be pushed to the very edge of the disc before it can run. This is worst in a chase, when the thumb is slammed down. setStick (stealth/js/game.js lines 78-91) stores any landing past 55% of travel as an offset (stickOrg). That offset only shrinks when the thumb moves back toward the centre (line 85); pushing outward never reduces it. Measured on the 212px portrait stick: landing at the rim (68px) gives m=0.55, walk at 53px/s, and the knob drawn at 37px, 31px behind the thumb. Pushing out to 78px gives 0.70 and 88px gives 0.85, both still walks. The run only starts at 95px, the last 11px of the 106px disc. Landscape 188px stick: the run starts at 84 of 94px. So the dashed ring stops being the run line, and the knob visibly drifts away from the thumb. The 0.12s stickDownT gate on line 317 already prevents a run on the first touch, so the offset does not need to last. Fix: make the offset expire quickly. Store the last thumb position in setStick (lastCx/lastCy). In updatePlayer, once time - stickDownT > 0.2, decay it each frame: stickOrg.x *= Math.exp(-dt*6), same for y, then call setStick(lastCx, lastCy) so the knob and stick.x/y follow. A rim landing then turns into a run after about 0.5s of holding, while a gentle landing stays silent. If the owner wants it stricter, still let outward motion eat the offset: in the else-branch, when rl > stickOrg.len, also multiply stickOrg by 0.85 per pointermove.

pieces.gap: The camera only locks to the player once the player stands still. Until then it follows them on an exponential ease, so it trails and then settles after a stop, which breaks the owner's 'anchored, no settling after a stop' rule. Measured from a real intro with the thumb held at 75% (walking at 67px/s): in portrait the player sat at y=344.2 instead of the anchor y=332, and in landscape at y=207.5 instead of 195. view.locked stayed false the whole 3s walk. On release the floor slid 12px back over about 0.4s and only then locked (at 3.45s). The lag equals speed*zoom/rate (67*1.147/6 ≈ 12.8px), so a run gives about 23px. It happens every time you come back into play still moving: after the intro (a touch skips it and moves at once), after closing the map by pushing, and after a respawn. All of these set view.locked=false. The cause is in js/game.js updateView, around lines 1079-1084. The lock test `Math.hypot(tx - view.x, ty - view.y) * view.z < 1.5` can never pass while the target moves, because `view.x += (tx - view.x) * k` with rate 6 always trails a moving target. Fix: replace the exponential approach with a fixed-length ease measured relative to the moving target. On the first unlocked play frame, save `view.ease = { dx: view.x - tx, dy: view.y - ty, z0: view.z, t: 0 }`. Each frame: `t += dt; e = 1 - Math.pow(1 - Math.min(1, t / 0.35), 3); view.x = tx + dx * (1 - e); view.y = ty + dy * (1 - e); view.z = z0 * Math.pow(tz / z0, e)`. When t >= 0.35, set view.locked = true and clear view.ease. Keep the existing rate-2.6 ease for the intro's map-to-player zoom. Clear view.ease anywhere locked is set to false. Done this way, the player reaches the fixed anchor (195,332 in portrait; 332,195 in landscape) within 0.35s even while running, and it never drifts again.

If the thumb aims the player's centre 26-28px off the door's centreline (the square still half over the opening), the square grinds on the jamb for 0.4s at walk and about 1s at sneak before going in. Cause, in js/game.js updatePlayer (about lines 352-366): the doorway assist only fires when total movement is under `want * 0.14`. At a convex corner the distance field's gradient is radial, so the square creeps sideways a little each frame, the trigger never fires and the creep is slow. Fix: (1) Trigger on progress along the push, not total movement: `const ix = inp.x, iy = inp.y; const prog = (P.x - before.x) * ix + (P.y - before.y) * iy; if (want > 0.05 && prog < want * 0.5 && ...)`. Keep the 'stays put' reset only for the near-head-on case where it applies now. (2) Widen the probe to the full player radius plus margin: `for (let t = 2; t <= 14 && !bt; t += 2)`. (3) Nudge faster: `const st = Math.min(Math.abs(bt), want * 0.8) * Math.sign(bt)`. (4) Probe along the tangent that is perpendicular to the input direction (`tx = -iy, ty = ix`) rather than the field tangent, since at a corner the radial gradient points the wrong way. pieces.gap: Sliding along a wall still costs a lot of speed. game.js updatePlayer (~lines 375-396) only uses field.move's plain projection, so a push 40 degrees off head-on slides at 0.64 of walk speed and 20 degrees off at 0.34. Hugging a wall with a thumb that is roughly but not exactly parallel (the normal case on a phone) feels sticky and slow, and the doorway-slip assist only fires within ~39 degrees of head-on. Fix: after field.move, if the push was blocked (prog < want*0.9), the tangential share of the input is |t·inp| > 0.3 (t = wall tangent from field.grad(P.x,P.y)), and the player is touching the wall (field.sample(P.x,P.y) < P_R+0.5), top the step along t up to want*max(|t·inp|, 0.85). Concretely: compute the slid distance s along t; if s < want*0.85*sign, call field.move(P, t.x*(want*0.85 - s), t.y*(want*0.85 - s), P_R). Keep the existing 'head-on stays put' rule for |t·inp| < 0.3, so pushing straight into a wall still does nothing. Then the 40-degree slide reaches about 0.85 and 60 to 80 degrees are barely touched. **The main fix, in `stealth/js/game.js` `updateGuard`.** Your exact spec didn't work. With the 0.72 cap and the 1.4 turn, the escape still failed 14 of 14 times. A sideways sneak at 55 units is about 0.8–0.9 rad/s, which is slower than a 1.4 rad/s turn that keeps following you. And at meter 0.6 the 'sus' guard starts walking toward you, which turns it at 2.6 anyway. So I changed it like this:
- **Fill cap:** the meter fills at most 0.72 per second, so it takes at least 1.4s from empty. The instant '!' under 20 units is unchanged.
- **A '?' is a glance:** when the '?' goes up, the guard remembers where you were (`susAt`). Until its meter has peaked at 0.75, it turns at 1.4 rad/s toward that spot, not toward you, and only far enough to bring it within 0.3 rad of its gaze. It doesn't walk toward you yet.
- **Then it tracks:** once the meter has passed 0.75, it turns at 2.6 to follow you and walks your way, as before. This uses the peak, so it doesn't swing back to the old spot when the meter drops.
- **New ai-check case "close '?' sidestep":** it teleports the player 55 units out at the edge of a post's cone and sneaks sideways (stick 0.6, about 57 u/s) 0.15s after the '?'. It needs no chase on at least 5 of 6 tries.

Each guard rolls once per door, and doors restored at a checkpoint don't count. In my test, 6 of 40 walkers went to look; some placements had no clear view of the door.
- **G4, shades by posts:** no shade's rim is closer than 60 units to a sentry. Across 686 shades on floors 4–14, the closest is exactly 60.

pieces.gap: G5: upper floors don't get harder, and the loose fallback lets through floors with almost nobody watching. In stealth/js/level.js, generate() turns on `loose` after attempt 3 (`attempt >= 3`, line ~219). Loose mode skips both the 'never thin' rejection (line ~1038: `if (!loose && n >= 3 && L.guards.length + L.cams.length < U.clamp(Math.round(0.6 * budget), 3, 9)) return null;`) and the post top-up in placeGuards (line ~1756: `const target = n >= 3 && !loose ? ... : 0`). That is how run seed 5004 floor 14 ends up with 2 guards, 0 cameras and 3 keys across 11 rooms. Fix: (1) loosen later, at `attempt >= 8`. (2) Keep a floor in loose mode as well: `target = n >= 3 ? U.clamp(Math.round((loose ? 0.5 : 0.7) * budget), 3, loose ? 8 : 12) : 0`, and use the same numbers in the reject at line ~1038. (3) Set a camera floor: from n >= 6, at least `1 + Math.floor((n - 6) / 5)` cameras, so 1 at f6-10, 2 at f11-15 and 3 at f16+, using the camera placer that is already there. (4) Base the watcher budget on area so density keeps rising: `budget = Math.min(D.budget, Math.round(4 + n * 0.8), Math.round(area/100k * (0.9 + 0.03 * n)))`, with D.budget raised to 15 at n ≥ 10. **G5 changes (level.js)**
- **Loose mode starts later:** `generate()` now turns it on at `attempt >= 8` instead of 3.
- **Shared rules:** three new helpers are used by both `placeGuards()` and the thin-floor reject in `tryGen()`, so the two always agree.
  - `watchBudget(L, n)` is your area formula: `min(D.budget, round(4+0.8n), round(area/100k*(0.9+0.03n)))`.
  - `watchFloor` is 0.7×budget clamped 3-12 normally, or 0.5×budget clamped 3-8 in loose mode.
  - `camFloor` is 1 camera at f6-10, 2 at f11-15, 3 from f16.
- **`D.budget`:** 15 at f10, then one more every two floors, capped at 19. With only the flat 15, every floor from f14 up got the same budget, so the median stopped rising. I capped it at 19 because each step up makes floors slower to build.
- **Camera floor:** I moved the existing camera placer into a reusable `camIn(room)`. When a floor is short of cameras, they go up in rooms that can take one. If the timing checks take a camera down and the floor drops below its share, it goes up again in another room.
- **The 70% floor alone wasn't enough:** the timing checks were taking walkers down until floors sat right at 70%. So the top-up now fills to the full budget, and walkers removed early in the retries are replaced with posts up to the budget. Late retries can still thin a floor to 70%.
- **Your repro seeds now build full floors:** 5004 f14 has 9 guards, 4 cameras; 5026 f14 15/6; 5004 f16 12/3; 5011 f16 10/3; 5028 f12 12/2.

**Results (15 seeds, guards + cameras)**

| Floor | Median before | Median after |
|---|---|---|
| f6 | 8 | 9 |
| f8 | 8 | 10 |
| f10 | 9 | 11 |
| f12 | 11 | 13 |

- **Not met:** the median does not rise every two floors. It sits at 12 on f14-15 and dips to 14 on f19, because the timing checks take most of the added guards back down there.

pieces.fix:
I changed only stealth/js/audio.js and committed nothing. Being caught now lands as the loudest hit in the game, and the stingers are in the right order. I measured this in the browser on the master output, using 0.4 s momentary loudness, both K-weighted and phone-weighted (4th-order high-pass at 550 Hz).

**Biggest gap: the caught sound and the stinger order**
- **Caught (`SFX.caught`):**
  - I added a phone-band impact: the [38,39,45] cluster two octaves up (about 300-440 Hz), each note as a detuned sawtooth plus square, lowpass 3500→500 Hz over 1.0 s.
  - The critic suggested v 0.16, dur 0.25. At those values it only reached about -10 LUFS, so I went to v 0.36, dur 0.42.
  - I added the crash noise (2200 Hz, q 0.6, v 0.6, dur 0.08, rel 0.7, falling to 500 Hz).
  - To make room in the headroom I cut the low sawtooth cluster from 0.18 to 0.1 and the kick from 0.45 to 0.3.
  - `cut()` now takes an optional delay, and caught calls `cut(1.6, 0.02)`, so the hit lands 20 ms before the score starts dropping out.
- **Pickups:** star, key and door now go to the `sfx` bus instead of `cue`, so cueLift no longer raises them in a chase. That bus skips the cue compressor and its built-in makeup gain, so I re-set their levels: star 0.16, key 0.24 (its noise 0.12), door about x1.5.

| Stinger alone | K-weighted (before → after) | Phone-weighted (after) |
|---|---|---|
| Caught | -12.4 → -8.5 | -11.9 |
| '!' | -12.6 | -14.6 |
| '?' | -12.8 | -13.2 |
| Star | -9.7 → -15.8 | -15.8 |
| Door | -14.1 → -16.0 | -21.0 |
| Key | -14.0 → -17.1 | -17.4 |

The order is now caught > '!' ≈ '?' > pickups. In a real scripted catch (floor 1, 95 px in front of a guard, suspicion, chase, caught), the chase ran at about -15 to -17 LUFS and the catch peaked at -9 to -9.6. That is 6-7 dB over the chase, where before the sound only faded away. The -8 target is not quite met: peaks are already at -2.1 dBFS, just short of the soft clipper (-1.94), so more level wasn't available.
